summary: @onereach/slack-helpers ships preinstall dropper that fetches Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: The npm package declares a Slack API helper purpose, but its package.json defines a preinstall hook (`node setup.mjs`) that downloads the Bun runtime from GitHub releases (bun-v1.3.13), extracts it to a temporary directory, marks it executable, and uses it to run a sibling file `math_init.js` — a 727KB heavily obfuscated blob (string-array/rotation obfuscator.io-style, marked `// @bun @bun-cjs`) that is not referenced by the declared main entry `dist/index.js`. The dist/ tree contains genuine Slack API code, so the obfuscated payload is unrelated to the advertised purpose. Using an alternate runtime (Bun) to execute the payload sidesteps Node-based inspection, and the obfuscation blocks review of what the payload actually does. Installing this package therefore results in arbitrary attacker-controlled code execution on the installer's machine at `npm install` time.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
